2.modern-en: Cassius sounds him out about Caesar's growing power. Brutus reveals he has been troubled by it. Agrees to consider the conspiracy.

4.modern-en: Alone in his orchard, decides that Caesar must die — not for what he is but for what he might become. Receives the conspirators and plans the assassination. Refuses to include Cicero or kill Antony.

8.modern-en: Stabs Caesar on the Senate steps. Addresses the senators, attempting to justify the act as a defense of liberty.

9.modern-en: Delivers his funeral oration to the crowd, explaining that he loved Caesar but loved Rome more. The crowd accepts his reasoning — until Antony speaks.

12.modern-en: Arrives at camp near Sardis with his army. Tension with Cassius over military strategy and the conduct of the war.

13.modern-en: Quarrels bitterly with Cassius in his tent, then reconciles. Learns of Portia's death. Sees Caesar's ghost, who promises to meet him at Philippi.

14.modern-en: Confronts Antony and Octavius before the battle of Philippi. Exchanges insults and farewells with Cassius.

18.modern-en: Defeated in battle, asks his servant to hold his sword and runs on it. Antony eulogizes him as 'the noblest Roman of them all.'

2.modern-en: Returns from the Lupercal. Ignores the soothsayer's warning to beware the Ides of March. Offered the crown three times by Antony and refuses each time.

5.modern-en: Disturbed by Calpurnia's dream of his murder. Agrees to stay home, then is persuaded by Decius to go to the Senate after all.

8.modern-en: Arrives at the Capitol. Refuses Artemidorus's petition. Stabbed by the conspirators, last by Brutus. Dies with the words 'Et tu, Brute?'

13.modern-en: Appears as a ghost in Brutus's tent, declaring 'Thou shalt see me at Philippi.'

2.modern-en: Offers Caesar the crown at the Lupercal. Runs in the Lupercalia race at Caesar's request.

8.modern-en: Sends a servant to test the conspirators' intentions, then appears in person. Shakes their bloody hands and privately vows revenge over Caesar's body.

9.modern-en: Delivers the funeral oration — 'Friends, Romans, countrymen' — turning the crowd against the conspirators by displaying Caesar's wounds and reading his will.

11.modern-en: Forms the triumvirate with Octavius and Lepidus. Coldly marks men for death in a proscription list.

14.modern-en: Commands the army at Philippi alongside Octavius. Confronts Brutus and Cassius before the battle.

18.modern-en: Finds Brutus's body and eulogizes him: 'This was the noblest Roman of them all.'

2.modern-en: Begins recruiting Brutus for the conspiracy, speaking of Caesar's physical weakness and the dishonor of submitting to one man's rule.

3.modern-en: Meets with Casca during a storm and confirms the conspiracy. Plans to leave forged letters where Brutus will find them.

4.modern-en: Joins the conspirators at Brutus's house. Overruled by Brutus on killing Antony and on swearing an oath.

8.modern-en: Participates in the assassination, stabbing Caesar.

12.modern-en: Arrives at Sardis, angry with Brutus over disagreements about discipline and money.

13.modern-en: Quarrels with Brutus, then reconciles. Overruled again on battle strategy — he wants to wait; Brutus insists on marching to Philippi.

16.modern-en: Believing the battle lost after Titinius is apparently captured, orders his servant Pindarus to kill him with the same sword that stabbed Caesar.

4.modern-en: Confronts Brutus about his sleeplessness and secrecy. Shows him a wound she inflicted on herself to prove she can bear suffering and keep a secret. Brutus promises to confide in her.

7.modern-en: Anxiously waits at home on the morning of the assassination, barely able to contain her knowledge of the plot.

13.modern-en: Her death is reported to Brutus — she swallowed fire, unable to bear his absence and the political crisis.
